questions.title: Junction between corona radiata and oocyte
questions.question: The junction between the cytoplasmic processes of the corona radiata cells and the microvilli of the oocyte is a:

explanations.A: Incorrect. A tight junction seals the space between epithelial cells and does not permit the metabolic coupling seen between the corona cells and the oocyte.
explanations.B: Incorrect. A desmosome is a mechanical anchoring junction and does not transfer ions or signalling molecules.
explanations.C: Incorrect. An adherens junction anchors actin filaments and does not provide the communication between the corona cells and the oocyte.
explanations.D: Correct. The corona radiata cells send processes across the zona pellucida to meet the oocyte microvilli, forming gap (communicating) junctions. These channels let ions, metabolites and signalling molecules pass directly between the follicular cells and the oocyte, nourishing it and helping to keep it arrested in meiosis until the LH surge.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the corona radiata-oocyte contact as a gap junction.

field_notes.keySource: printed p.29 Department answer table (Female Department Q9 = d)

questions.title: Timing of the first meiotic division
questions.question: In the female, the first meiotic division is completed:

explanations.A: Incorrect. It is the second meiotic division, not the first, that is completed only after fertilisation.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The first division is not completed early; the primary oocyte stays arrested in prophase I until just before ovulation.
explanations.C: Correct. The primary oocyte is arrested in prophase of the first meiotic division from fetal life until the LH surge, just before ovulation, lets it complete meiosis I to form a secondary oocyte and the first polar body. The secondary oocyte then arrests in metaphase II and completes the second division only if fertilised. Thus meiosis I finishes just before ovulation.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Puberty reactivates cyclical follicle growth but does not itself complete meiosis I in a given oocyte; completion occurs just before that oocyte's ovulation.

questions.learning_objective: State that meiosis I completes just before ovulation and meiosis II only after fertilisation.

field_notes.keySource: printed p.29 Dr Zahra answer table (Female Q8 = C); Q13 = C (second meiotic division completed after fertilisation) corroborates

questions.title: Lining of the oviduct wall
questions.question: The wall of the oviduct (fallopian tube):

options.A: Is lined by cells with cilia together with secretory cells
options.B: Is lined by non-ciliated columnar cells only
options.C: Is highly folded throughout the intramural portion
options.D: Is covered by adventitia (no peritoneal covering)

explanations.A: Correct. The oviduct mucosa is a simple columnar epithelium of two cell types: ciliated cells, whose cilia beat toward the uterus to move the ovum, and non-ciliated peg (secretory) cells, which produce fluid that nourishes the ovum and activates sperm. Both cell types are present, so the epithelium is ciliated and secretory. The mucosa is most folded in the ampulla, where fertilisation usually occurs.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The lining is not purely non-ciliated; ciliated cells are a key component.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The mucosal folds are most elaborate in the ampulla and least in the intramural (uterine) part, not highly folded throughout the intramural portion.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The fallopian tube is largely intraperitoneal and covered by serosa (peritoneum), not simply adventitia.

questions.learning_objective: Describe the oviduct lining as simple columnar epithelium of ciliated and peg (secretory) cells.

questions.title: Territory of the spiral arteries
questions.question: Concerning the spiral arteries of the endometrium, which statement is correct?

options.A: They supply the maturing ovarian follicles
options.C: They supply the endometrial basal zone
options.D: They supply the endometrial functional zone

explanations.A: Incorrect. Ovarian follicles are supplied by ovarian and uterine artery branches, not by the endometrial spiral arteries.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The corpus luteum is supplied by ovarian vessels, not by endometrial spiral arteries.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The basal zone is supplied by the short straight (basal) arteries, which are not shed; this preserves the regenerative basal layer.
explanations.D: Correct. The coiled spiral arteries extend into the functional zone of the endometrium, which thickens through the cycle and is shed at menstruation. Constriction of these hormone-sensitive spiral arteries causes the ischaemia that sheds the functional zone, while the straight-artery-supplied basal zone is spared.

questions.learning_objective: Match spiral arteries to the functional zone and straight arteries to the basal zone of the endometrium.

field_notes.keySource: printed p.29 Dr Zahra answer table (Female Q31 = D); Q45 = B and Q37 = D (basal zone supplied by straight arteries) corroborate

questions.title: Glands of the vaginal wall
questions.question: Concerning the vagina, which one of the following statements is correct?

options.C: It is vascular and has no glands

explanations.A: Incorrect. The vaginal wall has no mucous glands; its surface mucus comes from the cervix above.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The vagina has no serous glands either; it is a glandless mucosa.
explanations.C: Correct. The vagina is lined by non-keratinised stratified squamous epithelium and contains no glands. It is kept moist by cervical mucus and by transudate from its highly vascular, elastic-rich lamina propria, so 'vascular and without glands' is the correct description. Its acidic pH is produced by lactobacilli acting on epithelial glycogen, not by glands.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Because the vagina genuinely is a glandless, vascular mucosa, option C is correct and 'none of the above' cannot be selected.

questions.learning_objective: State that the vagina has no glands and is lubricated by cervical mucus and its vascular wall.

field_notes.keySource: printed p.29 Dr Zahra answer table (Female Q36 = C)
